name: Walt Disney Concert Hall
notes: The article is a tribute to Gehry, placed on the site at Los Angeles, so this models his Los Angeles landmark, the Walt Disney Concert Hall (2003). The photos do include it: one exterior of the entrance corner at dusk, showing the two tall stainless-steel sails, the lower sails curling out over the glass lobby, the rounded drum and the limestone podium with its broad stair and the curved lettering wall. The other photos are his buildings elsewhere (Bilbao, Fondation Louis Vuitton, the Dancing House, Pritzker Pavilion, MoPOP, Bard, Biomuseo, the Eisenhower Memorial) and a Los Angeles KFC, which were not modelled. Only that one view exists, so the back and sides of the hall, the plan, the podium garden and the heights (tallest sails ~44 m) are guessed from general knowledge of the building; the entrance corner is faced south, not to the real street grid. Each sail is a flaring arc of steel, drawn as stacked one-metre boxes (the part types have no curved sheet), with the roofs between them in metal and concrete.
